clarification.before:
CLD Corollary 15.2.9: if $F$
   is a closed subset countable at infinity (in particular compact) of
   such a space and $(U_i)$ is an ordinary open cover of $F$, there are
   nonnegative ordinary smooth functions $\chi_i$, locally finite,
   compactly supported in their respective $U_i$, with
   $\sum_i\chi_i=1$ near $F$. Only finite covers of compact sets are
   used here.
clarification.after: For a compact subset $F$ and a finite ordinary open cover $(U_i)$ of $F$, there are nonnegative ordinary smooth $\theta_i$, each compactly supported inside $U_i$, with $\sum_i\theta_i=1$ near $F$. This compact specialization follows from CLD Corollary 15.2.5 and ordinary smooth functional calculus. For each $x\in F$, apply 15.2.5 with $\{x\}\subset U_i$ to obtain a smooth function equal to one near $x$ and compactly supported in $U_i$. Compose with a nonnegative smooth real function equal to zero near zero and equal to one near one, obtaining a nonnegative bump with the same support containment. Compactness selects finitely many such bumps; group them by cover index into $\psi_i$, and put $s=\sum_i\psi_i$. Then $s>0$ near $F$. Apply 15.2.5 again to compact $F$ inside the open $\{s>0\}$, and the same nonnegative composition, to obtain $\chi$ compactly supported there and equal to one near $F$. Set $\theta_i=\chi\psi_i/s$ on that open and extend by zero. Smoothness follows since the support of $\chi$ lies compactly inside the open. Each $\theta_i$ has compact support inside $U_i$ and their sum is $\chi$. No arbitrary countable-at-infinity, fixed-cover-index compact-support assertion is used. Only this compact-set, finite-cover version is needed.
clarification.application_before:
Take fixed cutoffs $\chi_i$ from CLD 15.2.9, compactly supported in
$U_i$
clarification.application_after:
Take fixed cutoffs $\chi_i$ from the compact finite-cover construction
in Section 2(4), using CLD 15.2.5, compactly supported in $U_i$
clarification.reason: Compact cutoff specialization actually used; no theorem or actual use changed
